title: External status protocol and runbook for multi-tenant incidents
author: Aisha Patel
body:
SUMMARY
This playbook defines the external status protocols, approved customer communication templates, and operational runbook for multi-tenant incidents that impact Redwood Inference hosted APIs or Dedicated clusters. It is intended for oncall engineers, SRE bridge operators, customer success, and incident commanders.

SCOPE AND INTENDED USE
- Applies to incidents where one or more customers experience degraded latency, errors, or data-loss risk from hosted API, Dedicated, or Private deployments with observable customer impact.
- Excludes purely internal developer outages with zero customer-facing impact (see internal-only runbook).
- Use when incident severity >= S2 (see Severity mapping).

OWNERSHIP AND ROLES
- Incident Commander (IC): oncall SRE or senior engineer (primary decision-maker for containment and external comms).
- Bridge Operator: runs the incident bridge and coordinates cross-team contributors.
- Customer Success Lead (CSL): owns customer-facing messaging and coordinates targeted customer outreach for impacted tenants.
- Model Owner / Serving Team: owners of the model-serving stack (model-serving team).
- Communications Reviewer: product marketing or legal for escalated enterprise disclosures (if required).

SEVERITY MAPPING (quick reference)
- S1 — Critical: Broad outage impacting >20% of requests or >5 customers with >30% error rates for >5 minutes. Triggers immediate exec alert and public status page incident.
- S2 — Major degradation: Significant latency or error rate increase for a subset of customers (>5% of requests or 1–5 customers affected) for >15 minutes. Triggers status page incident and targeted customer notices.
- S3 — Minor or single-customer impact: Latency or quality regressions affecting a single customer or non-critical degradation (work with CS for customer notice).

SLOs / ALERT THRESHOLDS (service-level examples)
| Service | SLO (p99 latency) | Alert threshold | Error budget policy |
| inference-gateway | 300 ms | p99 > 1200 ms for 5m | Pause non-critical experiments at 50% burn |
| model-serving | 75 ms per-token | p99 > 500 ms for 2m | Auto-fallback to smaller variant at 75% burn |
| router-api | 200 ms | p99 > 800 ms for 10m | Scale routing pods; escalate to infra |
NOTE: Table above is a plain-text representation — use monitoring dashboards for current SLO telemetry.

INITIAL BRIDGE AND RESPONSE PROCEDURE (first 15 minutes)
1) Acknowledge: PagerDuty/Slack alert acknowledged by first responder in 2 minutes.
2) Bridge up: Bridge Operator creates incident bridge (Zoom + Slack channel) and posts initial summary. Use channel name: #bridge-<short-service>-YYYYMMDD-HHMM.
3) Triage: IC classifies severity (S1/S2/S3) within 10 minutes and assigns roles.
4) Customer signal: CSL prepares initial status page and customer notification drafts using templates below.
5) Containment plan: list immediate mitigations (see containment checklist).
6) Evidence capture: collect logs, traces, backend metrics, and top-50 request traces to evidence bucket (S3 path pattern: s3://redwood-incident-evidence/<incident-id>/).

CONTAINMENT CHECKLIST (pick applicable steps quickly)
- Fail open to bulkhead-similar region: route traffic to fallback-region (region fallback policy).
- Activate model fallback: switch traffic from large-llm to quantized or smaller variant via router-api: POST /control/fallback?service=model-serving&variant=lite.
- Increase autoscaling target for inference-gateway by +50% (k8s HPA or cluster autoscaler).
- Disable non-essential batch jobs (analytics-ingest, background-aggregator) to free GPU/CPU.
- Purge or temporarily bypass KV cache if stale/poisoned: cache-ops flush-key-prefix --prefix=user-cache-<tenant-id>.

EXTERNAL STATUS PAGE PROCESS
- When to publish: Publish to public status page for any S1 and S2 incidents; optional for S3 when multiple customers affected.
- Status page ownership: Bridge Operator initiates the status update; CSL reviews before publish.
- Frequency: initial update within 15 minutes of incident classification; follow-ups every 30 minutes while active, then every 2 hours during stabilization; final resolution update when incident is resolved and postmortem scheduled.

PUBLIC STATUS TEMPLATES (replace tokens in {{double-braces}})
- Initial (S1/S2):
  Title: Degraded performance for Redwood inference API - detection ongoing
  Body: We are investigating increased error rates and elevated latency for the Redwood Inference API that may affect model responses and embeddings for some customers. Our oncall team has identified impacted regions: {{regions}} and is actively working on mitigation. No data loss has been detected at this time. Next update: in 30 minutes or sooner. Incident ID: {{incident-id}}.

- Update (stabilizing):
  Title: Mitigation in progress — partial recovery observed
  Body: We have implemented mitigations ({{mitigation-actions}}) and are seeing partial recovery in {{regions}}. Some requests may still experience increased latency. We will continue monitoring and provide another update by {{time}}. A targeted customer notice has been sent to affected tenants.

- Resolved:
  Title: Incident resolved — service normal
  Body: The incident impacting {{services}} has been resolved at {{timestamp}}. All systems are operating within normal parameters and SLOs are recovering. We are scheduling a post-incident report and will reach out to any customers who experienced sustained impact.

CUSTOMER EMAIL / CSR TEMPLATE (targeted notice for impacted customers)
Subject: Service impact affecting your Redwood Inference requests — incident {{incident-id}}
Body: Hello {{customer-name}},

We detected an incident that affected your requests between {{start}} and {{end}} against {{service-or-route}}. Our team applied the following mitigations: {{mitigation-actions}}. Based on initial analysis, the incident resulted in {{high-level-impact}} (e.g., higher latency, partial errors). We will follow up with a post-incident summary and actionable recommendations within 72 hours. If you need an immediate technical lead, reply and we will schedule a dedicated call.

RUNBOOK: TROUBLESHOOTING MATRIX (by symptom)
- Symptom: High p99 latency on inference-gateway  Causes to check: CPU saturation on gateway pods, network egress issues, backend model-serving queue depth > 500.  Steps: 1) kubectl top pods -n serving | sort -r; 2) check gateway logs for 502/504 spikes; 3) scale replicas: kubectl scale deploy inference-gateway --replicas=<current*1.5>.
- Symptom: Increased 5xx from model-serving  Causes: model process crashes, OOM errors, model KV cache poisoning.  Steps: 1) check pod restarts: kubectl get pods -n model-serving -o wide; 2) inspect logs /var/log/model-serve.log; 3) roll model instance: /ops/rollout model-serving --selector=canary=false --max-surge=1.
- Symptom: Erratic user-specific errors  Causes: tenant config changes, prompt injection, corrupted tenant cache.  Steps: 1) isolate tenant traffic by routing to a dedicated lane; 2) flush tenant KV cache; 3) open high-priority support ticket to CSL.

ESCALATION MATRIX
- If containment not achieved within 30 minutes for S1: escalate to Head of SRE and oncall infra; issue an exec notification (email + Slack #exec-alerts).
- If third-party dependency (e.g., cloud provider networking) is suspected: open a provider support ticket and attach incident evidence bundle immediately.
- For potential data exposure: pause customer notifications until Security is engaged and legal is consulted (see security-and-compliance data-exposure SOP).

POST-INCIDENT ACTIONS AND EVIDENCE RETENTION
1) Immediate capture: store logs/traces and a short incident chronology in s3://redwood-incident-evidence/<incident-id>/chronology.txt.
2) Postmortem draft: IC + Bridge Operator draft within 72 hours. Use postmortem template: executive summary, timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigation and long-term fixes, owners, ETA.
3) Evidence retention: retain raw traces for 90 days, aggregate metrics for 1 year. PII or customer-sensitive logs are archived with restricted access.
4) Customer follow-up: CSL to send tailored postmortem or summary within 72 hours to impacted customers, and schedule one-on-one calls for enterprise accounts as needed.

ONCALL ROTATION AND HANDOFFS (practical notes)
- Primary oncall: 7x24 primary rotation with 1-week shifts. Secondary oncall: 1-week shadow rotation for escalations.
- Handover checklist: unresolved incidents, active mitigations, pending postmortem actions, customer callbacks scheduled, links to active bridges. Use the template: Handover: <incidents>, <actions>, <blocked-by>.
- Escalation points: if primary cannot make a decision within 20 minutes, the secondary steps in as IC.

GAME DAY EXERCISES (recommended cadence)
- Quarterly full-scale game day that simulates a multi-tenant latency storm affecting router-api + model-serving. Objective: practice status page cadence, targeted customer comms, and model-fallback automation.
- Focused exercises monthly for new joiners to practice bridge operator responsibilities and evidence capture.

METRICS FOR COMMUNICATION (what to include in updates)
- Impacted customers count and representative tenant IDs (anonymized for public updates).
- % of requests failing and p99 latency relative to baseline.
- Mitigations applied and immediate effect (e.g., p99 improved from 1.4s -> 420ms).

AUDIT AND APPROVALS
- All public status updates must be approved by IC and CSL before publishing. For enterprise customers, postmortem and remediation plan must be reviewed by Security if data exposure or regulatory impact is suspected.

APPENDIX: CLI SNIPPETS AND LINKS
- Create bridge (internal tool): rwi bridge create --service model-serving --severity S1 --owner @aisha
- Evidence bundle upload: rwi incident evidence upload --id {{incident-id}} --path /tmp/evidence.tar.gz --s3 s3://redwood-incident-evidence/{{incident-id}}/
- Model fallback trigger (internal API): curl -X POST https://control.redwood.internal/rollout/fallback -d '{"service":"model-serving","variant":"lite"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'

DOCUMENT HISTORY AND NOTES
- Created: 2026-03-15 by Aisha Patel
- Major revision: 2026-09-10 — added customer email templates and clarified evidence retention policy.

END OF DOCUMENT
